text: Mongán was an Irish hero. He ruled as a king in the seventh century CE, yet he stayed partly mythological. He was said to be the son of the sea god Manannán Mac Lir. His name, which means hairy fellow, was given him because he was born with a full head of hair. From his father he inherited the talent of shape-shifting. He could also move between this world and the Otherworld. His divine father conceived him by disguising himself as a human king. That motif parallels the conception of King Arthur. Mongán was described as the reincarnation of the Irish hero Fionn mac Cumhaill. Fionn's fair wife Gráinne ran off with the hero Diarmait. That story parallels the tale of Guinevere and Lancelot. So however historical his reign, Mongán seems to reflect an ancient Celtic tale of the goddess of Sovereignty.
objective: Document the Irish hero Mongán and his mythological traits.
